groups.label: Control
groups.blurb: How the agent should behave on this task. Put these first when you care about the shape of the work.

groups.label: Read
groups.blurb: Look before touching. Use these when you want a map, a trace, or an explanation instead of a change.

groups.label: Build
groups.blurb: Make the change in the codebase that already exists. Match its patterns.

groups.label: Repair
groups.blurb: Find the cause, fix that, and leave a check behind. No drive-by cleanup.

groups.label: Ship
groups.blurb: Prove it works, including on a phone, and say what's left in plain language.

groups.label: Research
groups.blurb: Separate what was found from what was guessed. Keep the source next to the claim.

groups.label: Write
groups.blurb: Spec, rewrite, and the messages around the work. Keep the meaning you already have.

groups.label: Design
groups.blurb: Screens, layout, and critique. One primary action. Use the tokens that are already there.

groups.label: Picture
groups.blurb: Direction for a still or a clip. The picture book has the rest of the visual codes.

groups.label: Browser
groups.blurb: Operate a page you name. Don't wander, don't sign in, don't guess missing fields.

groups.label: Study
groups.blurb: Teach, quiz, and drill. One question at a time when the command says to wait.

groups.label: Decide
groups.blurb: Options, a call, and the risks. Say what would change the answer.

entries.meaning: Restate the job, the done-condition, and what you will not touch.
entries.when: The task is fuzzy, or you want the agent to show it understood before editing.
entries.avoid: Don't start editing in the same breath. Don't widen the job.
steps: Restate the job in one short paragraph.
State the done-condition as something you can check.
List what is out of scope.
Continue only if nothing material is ambiguous. Otherwise ask one question.
entries.example: Add a saved-filters view to the list. Don't redesign the navigation.

entries.meaning: Write the plan only. No edits, no installs, no servers.
entries.when: You want the approach before any file changes.
entries.avoid: Don't implement 'while you're in there.' Don't pad the plan with optional ideas.
steps: Name the files you expect to touch.
Name the risks and how you'll check the result.
entries.example: Plan how you'll add offline starring without an account.

entries.meaning: Carry out the plan you already have.
entries.when: A plan exists and you want it executed, not reopened.
entries.avoid: Don't relitigate the plan unless a step is blocked.
steps: If a step is blocked, stop and say why.
Don't add steps that were not in the plan.
entries.example: Go. The plan we agreed is the one in your last message.

entries.meaning: Change only what the task needs.
entries.when: You want a fix or feature without a cleanup tour.
entries.avoid: Don't refactor neighbors, rename for taste, or add settings nobody asked for.
steps: Touch the smallest set of files that solves the task.
Leave unrelated code as you found it.
If you notice a separate issue, mention it. Don't fix it.
entries.example: The empty state says 'No items' even when the request failed. Fix the copy only.

entries.meaning: State your assumptions, pick the safest, and continue.
entries.when: A few details are open but you don't want a questionnaire.
entries.avoid: Don't stop for a preference you can default safely. Don't hide a risky assumption.
steps: Mark the one you are using.
entries.example: Add export. Proceed if I didn't name the format.

entries.meaning: Ask the single question that unblocks you, then stop.
entries.when: You are actually blocked, not merely missing a preference.
entries.avoid: Don't ask a stack of questions. Don't keep working past the block.
steps: Offer two to four concrete options.
entries.example: Ask before you pick a database. I haven't decided.

entries.meaning: Report done, in progress, blocked, and the next step.
entries.when: You want a snapshot, not more work.
entries.avoid: Don't teach. Don't start the next step.
steps: Use four labels: done, in progress, blocked, next.
One to three lines under each, or 'none.'
entries.example: Status on the filter work.

entries.meaning: Stop this approach. Say what changed and what you did not verify.
entries.when: The current attempt is wrong and you don't want it stacked on.
entries.avoid: Don't keep patching the failed approach.
entries.example: Stop. The animation approach is wrong.

entries.meaning: The lines under this command outrank your defaults.
entries.when: You have rules that should beat helpful extras.
entries.avoid: Don't 'improve' past a constraint.
steps: Read the constraints under this command as binding.
If one conflicts with a habit of yours, follow the constraint.
If two constraints conflict, say so and stop.
entries.example:
Constraints:
Keep the lime accent.
No new dependencies.
No accounts.

entries.meaning: Use the fewest words that are still complete.
entries.when: You want the answer, not a tour of the reasoning.
entries.avoid: Don't drop the result, the decision, or a real blocker just to be short.
steps: Keep the one detail that would be dangerous to omit.
entries.example: Quiet. What file owns the search ranking?

entries.meaning: Lead with the thing the user can use.
entries.when: The user wants the result, not how the tools were used.
entries.avoid: Don't narrate plumbing, ports, or internal steps unless asked.
steps: Then the one next action, if there is one.
entries.example: Show me the empty state you wrote.

entries.meaning: Pause after this step and show the result before continuing.
entries.when: You want to approve a step before the rest happens.
entries.avoid: Don't run ahead after the checkpoint.
steps: Do only the step in front of you.
entries.example: Checkpoint after the data shape, before any UI.

entries.meaning: Map only the parts of the system this task touches.
entries.when: You don't know where the behavior lives yet.
entries.avoid: Don't tour unrelated trees. Don't propose a rewrite in the map.
steps: Follow the data from input to the screen or response.
List the files that matter, each with why.
entries.example: Codemap the path from search box to the filtered list.

entries.meaning: Find every place that owns this behavior.
entries.when: You need the call sites, not a folder.
entries.avoid: Don't list files that only mention the word.
steps: Name the file and the symbol.
Say whether it is the owner or a caller.
Stop when the set is complete.
entries.example: Find what decides the star is filled.

entries.meaning: Walk the execution path and name where state goes wrong.
entries.when: Something behaves oddly and you want the path, not a fix yet.
entries.avoid: Don't fix it in this pass unless a later command says so.
steps: Mark the hop where the result diverges from what should happen.
entries.example: Trace what happens when the query is cleared.

entries.meaning: Explain what the code is doing, in plain language.
entries.when: You want to understand a piece before changing it.
entries.avoid: Don't narrate line by line. Don't suggest a rewrite unless asked.
steps: Say why it is shaped this way, if the code shows that.
Name the trap a caller could hit.
entries.example: Explaincode the rank function.

entries.meaning: List the invariants this code must keep.
entries.when: You are about to change something that has silent rules.
entries.avoid: Don't invent rules the code doesn't honor. Mark guesses.
steps: Mark which ones have a test.
Mark which ones are only implied.
entries.example: Contracts for the brief stack. It caps at six.

entries.meaning: Name what this change depends on, and what breaks if those move.
entries.when: You want the coupling before you edit.
entries.avoid: Don't propose replacing the dependency unless asked.
steps: Name the callers and screens that feel a break.
entries.example: Deps if I change the command id format.

entries.meaning: Explain what a change does and why it matters.
entries.when: You have a diff and want it in plain language.
entries.avoid: Don't review yet unless asked. Don't restate every line.
steps: Say what the user can do now that they couldn't.
Say what behavior stayed the same.
Name anything the diff claims that it does not do.
entries.example: Diff the uncommitted work.

entries.meaning: Name the blast radius of this change.
entries.when: The edit looks small and you want to know what else moves.
entries.avoid: Don't inflate it into a rewrite proposal.
steps: List callers, stored data, and UI that can change behavior.
Mark the ones you will recheck.
entries.example: Blast if the star key in local storage changes.

entries.meaning: Build the agreed behavior in the style of this codebase.
entries.when: The behavior is decided and you want it built.
entries.avoid: Don't redesign the surrounding product. Don't leave it unwired.
steps: Wire it into the real entry, not a side demo.
Include the states the screen actually has.
entries.example: Implement the brief composer we specced.

entries.meaning: Add only the files this feature needs, and wire them in.
entries.when: You are starting a feature that doesn't have a home yet.
entries.avoid: Don't generate a parallel app inside the app.
steps: Create the smallest set of files.
Register them where the app already routes or renders.
Use the existing tokens and types.
entries.example: Scaffold a detail sheet for one command.

entries.meaning: Connect the pieces that already exist.
entries.when: The parts are built and the link between them is missing.
entries.avoid: Don't redesign the pieces while connecting them.
steps: Connect them with the data they already speak.
Prove the path with one real case.
entries.example: Wire Saved so it shows starred commands from this book.

entries.meaning: Add state using the pattern this app already uses.
entries.when: The interaction needs memory the UI doesn't have.
entries.avoid: Don't add a new state library. Don't lift state higher than it needs to go.
steps: Use the existing store or component state.
Persist only if the behavior is supposed to survive reload.
entries.example: State for the brief, capped at six command ids.

entries.meaning: Design a small, consistent interface for the task.
entries.when: You need a function, route, or component API.
entries.avoid: Don't add options for imaginary callers. Don't return fake success.
steps: Match the style of the neighboring interface.
entries.example: API for copying either one command or a whole brief.

entries.meaning: Change the data shape without destroying what's already stored.
entries.when: Saved data on device or in a table has to move.
entries.avoid: Don't wipe storage unless the task says to.
steps: Accept both shapes, or migrate on read.
Say what happens to data you can't read.
entries.example: Migrate starred ids if the command slug changes.

entries.meaning: Add or tighten types without changing behavior.
entries.when: The types are lying or too loose.
entries.avoid: Don't cast away an error you don't understand. Don't change runtime behavior.
steps: Make the type match what the code actually does.
entries.example: Types for the group id on a command.

entries.meaning: Propose clearer names for unclear symbols.
entries.when: A name is hiding what the thing does.
entries.avoid: Don't rename the world. Don't pick cute names.
steps: Rename only the symbols in this task if the task says to apply it.
entries.example: Naming for the function that builds the paste text.

entries.meaning: Include the empty, loading, and error states.
entries.when: A screen only handles the happy path.
entries.avoid: Don't leave a blank while data is missing. Don't use a joke as the error.
steps: Say what the user sees when there is nothing.
Say what they see while it loads, if loading is real.
Say what they can do when it fails.
entries.example: Empty states for search with no hits.

entries.meaning: Find the closest existing pattern and follow it.
entries.when: You want the new UI to feel like the rest of the app.
entries.avoid: Don't introduce a second visual language.
steps: Name the file you are matching.
Follow its structure, type, and spacing.
Differ only where the new behavior requires it.
entries.example: Pattern the new list on the existing code list.

entries.meaning: Merge parallel work into one coherent app.
entries.when: Two changes grew separately and need to become one.
entries.avoid: Don't average conflicting designs. Pick the one that fits the app.
steps: Check the joined path still works.
entries.example: Integrate the command book with the picture book navigation.

entries.meaning: If a behavior must be optional, default it to today's behavior.
entries.when: You are adding something people should be able to ignore.
entries.avoid: Don't turn the flag on by default if that changes current users.
entries.example: Flags for showing examples on the list rows. Off by default.

entries.meaning: Restructure the code without changing behavior.
entries.when: The structure is blocking the task, and behavior must stay.
entries.avoid: Don't mix a refactor with a feature. Don't 'improve' behavior along the way.
steps: State the behavior that must stay.
Check the behavior is the same.
entries.example: Refactor the sheet so both books can use it. Same look.

entries.meaning: Reduce branching and indirection while keeping behavior.
entries.when: The code is harder to follow than the job it does.
entries.avoid: Don't remove a branch that handles a real case.
steps: Remove a layer only if no caller needs it.
entries.example: Simplifycode the filter logic.

entries.meaning: Find the likely bug. Name the cause, then fix the cause.
entries.when: Something fails and you want it actually fixed.
entries.avoid: Don't patch the symptom. Don't clean unrelated code.
steps: Reproduce it with the smallest case.
Name the cause in one sentence.
Show the check that now passes.
entries.example: The save button stays disabled after the form is valid.

entries.meaning: Turn a bug report into the smallest steps that reproduce it.
entries.when: You have a vague report and need a recipe.
entries.avoid: Don't fix it yet if this command is alone.
steps: State what you expect and what happens.
Cut any step that isn't needed to show the bug.
entries.example: People say search sometimes shows picture codes inside the agent book.

entries.meaning: List the inputs most likely to break this.
entries.when: You want the cases before or after a fix.
entries.avoid: Don't list theoretical cases that this code cannot receive.
steps: List the cases that can actually happen here.
Say the expected result for each.
Mark the ones that fail today, if you know.
entries.example: Edgecases for the brief when it is full.

entries.meaning: Narrow it to the smallest case that still fails.
entries.when: The failure is real but the area is large.
entries.avoid: Don't speculate a cause before the case is small.
steps: Find the last known good behavior, if you can.
Shrink the input until removing anything makes the bug vanish.
entries.example: Bisect why copying fails only on the phone preview.

entries.meaning: Apply the fix. Keep the diff to the bug.
entries.when: The cause is known.
entries.avoid: Don't bundle a refactor. Don't claim it's fixed without a check.
steps: Change only what the cause requires.
Keep a check that fails before and passes after, when a check is possible.
entries.example: Fix the off-by-one when the sixth command is added.

entries.meaning: Write tests for the important paths and the edge cases.
entries.when: Behavior needs a lock so it doesn't regress.
entries.avoid: Don't test the framework. Don't assert copy you expect to keep changing, unless the copy is the contract.
steps: Cover the edge case that broke or is likely to.
entries.example: Tests for ranking an exact code match above a substring.

entries.meaning: Check the neighbors this change could have broken.
entries.when: A fix landed and nearby behavior might have moved.
entries.avoid: Don't expand into a full rewrite of the neighbors.
entries.example: Regress starring and the picture book after the nav change.

entries.meaning: Review the code for bugs, risks, and concrete fixes.
entries.when: You want a picky pass, not more features.
entries.avoid: Don't nitpick taste. Don't rewrite the feature in the review.
steps: Look for correctness, security, and missing states.
Say the fix in one sentence.
Block only on those. Mention nits separately.
entries.example: Review the brief assembler.

entries.meaning: Review for injection, auth gaps, and data exposure.
entries.when: The change takes input, stores data, or crosses a trust boundary.
entries.avoid: Don't wave it through because it 'looks internal.'
steps: Check input handling, auth, and secrets.
Cite the line if something is wrong.
Say 'nothing in this change' if that's the truth.
entries.example: Security on the task text that gets pasted into the brief.

entries.meaning: Read the failure and quote the first real error.
entries.when: There is a stack trace or a long log.
entries.avoid: Don't anchor on the last line if it's fallout.
steps: Quote the first error that is a cause.
Ignore trailing noise unless it changes the cause.
entries.example: Logs from the failed build. Quote the real error.

entries.meaning: Explain the intermittence, then fix that.
entries.when: It fails sometimes.
entries.avoid: Don't add a sleep and call it fixed.
steps: Say whether it is order, time, shared state, or a real race.
Say how you'll know it stayed fixed.
entries.example: Flaky: the sheet sometimes opens the previous command.

entries.meaning: Back out the failed approach before trying the next one.
entries.when: An attempt made things worse.
entries.avoid: Don't stack the next idea on the failed one.
steps: Confirm the previous behavior is back.
Then try the next approach, if one was asked for.
entries.example: Undo the virtualized list. It broke tap targets.

entries.meaning: Improve the hot path. Leave the rest alone.
entries.when: Something is actually slow.
entries.avoid: Don't micro-optimize cold code. Don't change behavior.
steps: Say how you know it is cheaper.
entries.example: Optimize filtering when the query changes. The list is long.

entries.meaning: Run the checks that prove this works. Report pass or fail.
entries.when: You want evidence, not a feeling.
entries.avoid: Don't say it works if you didn't run the check.
steps: Report pass or fail with the signal.
If something wasn't run, say so.
entries.example: Verify search, starring, and copying a brief.

entries.meaning: Confirm the screen shows real content on a phone width and a laptop width.
entries.when: UI changed and you need to know it actually rendered.
entries.avoid: Don't trust a successful request alone. Don't ignore the console.
steps: Look at a narrow phone width and a laptop width.
Confirm the console has no uncaught errors.
entries.example: Preview the command list.

entries.meaning: Check names, keyboard, focus, and contrast for what you changed.
entries.when: The change has controls, especially icon buttons.
entries.avoid: Don't boil the ocean outside this change.
steps: Every icon button has a name.
entries.example: A11y on the add-to-brief buttons.

entries.meaning: At a phone width: no sideways scroll, no overlap, targets you can tap.
entries.when: Someone will use this on a phone.
entries.avoid: Don't shrink text below a readable size to force a fit.
entries.example: Mobile on the command list and the brief bar.

entries.meaning: Name the one cost that matters here.
entries.when: You suspect the screen or the query is heavy.
entries.avoid: Don't optimize anything except that cost.
steps: Say whether it matters at the size this product actually has.
Change it only if it does.
entries.example: Perf of rendering the full command list.

entries.meaning: Write what changed and what to try, in the user's words.
entries.when: You need a note a person can act on.
entries.avoid: Don't mention internal file names unless the user works in the repo.
steps: Say a limit if there is one.
entries.example: Changelog for the agent command book.

entries.meaning: Note how to run it, what is fragile, and what is not done.
entries.when: Someone else will pick this up, including future you.
entries.avoid: Don't write a manual. Don't hide a known gap.
entries.example: Handoff on the command book.

entries.meaning: Check the work against the done-condition. List any gap.
entries.when: You are about to call it finished.
entries.avoid: Don't call it done with a known gap buried in the middle.
steps: Mark each part met or not.
List gaps before you say finished.
entries.example: Done check for 'a full list of agent commands I can copy.'

entries.meaning: Add concise documentation for the public surface.
entries.when: A behavior is now part of how people use the product.
entries.avoid: Don't document internals. Don't drift from what the UI actually does.
steps: Document the surface a user touches.
Keep it shorter than the feature.
entries.example: Docs: how to build a brief and copy it.

entries.meaning: Look it up. Separate what you found from what you inferred.
entries.when: The answer depends on facts you shouldn't invent.
entries.avoid: Don't present memory as a current source. Don't skip the link.
steps: Put the source next to the claim.
entries.example: Research the current limit on brief length for this kind of prompt.

entries.meaning: Check factual claims and flag what could not be verified.
entries.when: A draft contains facts that might be wrong.
entries.avoid: Don't silently rewrite a claim you couldn't check. Flag it.
entries.example: Factcheck the sources paragraph in the picture book.

entries.meaning: Use current documentation. Say the version or the date.
entries.when: An API or product changes and memory may be stale.
entries.avoid: Don't answer from an old major version if the project is on a newer one.
steps: Read the docs that match the version in this project.
Say the version or date you used.
entries.example: Latest on how file routes are defined in this repo.

entries.meaning: Define the terms as this project uses them.
entries.when: Words like brief, code, and stack are overloaded.
entries.avoid: Don't substitute dictionary definitions for the product's.
steps: Define each as this product uses it.
Note a collision if the same word means two things here.
entries.example: Glossary for code, command, brief, and stack.

entries.meaning: Survey the options quickly. Go deep on the two that fit.
entries.when: You want a landscape, not a treatise.
entries.avoid: Don't give equal depth to options that are a bad fit.
steps: List the real options in a few lines each.
Go one level deeper on those.
entries.example: Scan ways to persist a brief on this device only.

entries.meaning: Map the actors, forces, and relationships.
entries.when: The question is about a system, not a single function.
entries.avoid: Don't turn it into an org chart of code files. That's codemap.
entries.example: Systemmap for a student, an examiner, and a drill.

entries.meaning: Work backward from the result to how it is produced.
entries.when: You can see the outcome and need the mechanism.
entries.avoid: Don't invent steps you didn't find.
steps: Mark any hop you could not confirm.
entries.example: Reverseengineer how a starred command survives reload.

entries.meaning: Write the spec: who it's for, the job, done-when, and out of scope.
entries.when: The work needs a contract before building.
entries.avoid: Don't include implementation trivia. Don't leave done-when as a vibe.
entries.example: Spec a full command list for my agent.

entries.meaning: Rephrase the text I give you. Keep the meaning.
entries.when: The words are close but the wording is wrong.
entries.avoid: Don't add claims, features, or a new tone I didn't ask for.
steps: Don't add a closer or a moral.
entries.example: Rewrite: 'This is a list of commands you can paste.'

entries.meaning: Condense it. Same facts.
entries.when: It's too long for the place it sits.
entries.avoid: Don't drop a number, a name, or a constraint to make it shorter.
steps: Cut about a third, more if it's fluffy.
entries.example: Shorten the group blurbs.

entries.meaning: Make it easier to understand, in plainer language.
entries.when: A smart non-expert has to act on it.
entries.avoid: Don't talk down. Don't remove the precise term if the plain word is wrong.
steps: Keep the term where precision matters, and define it once.
entries.example: Simplify the paragraph about briefs.

entries.meaning: Rewrite so it sounds natural, not like a template.
entries.when: The text sounds generated.
entries.avoid: Don't add slang, jokes, or fake warmth.
steps: Use sentences a person would say.
entries.example: Human the empty-state line.

entries.meaning: Change the tone to professional.
entries.when: The text will be seen in a formal place.
entries.avoid: Don't make it stiff. Don't add legalese it doesn't need.
entries.example: Formal the handoff note.

entries.meaning: Propose a commit message from the change. Don't commit unless asked.
entries.when: You want the message, not the commit.
entries.avoid: Don't commit or push. Don't mention files that didn't change.
steps: Body: why, if why isn't obvious.
entries.example: Commit-msg for the agent command book.

entries.meaning: Write the description: what, why, how to test, risk.
entries.when: The change needs a review note.
entries.avoid: Don't market it. Don't hide a risk.
entries.example: PR text for adding the command book.

entries.meaning: Write the message a person should see: what happened, and the next action.
entries.when: An error is currently a code or a blank.
entries.avoid: Don't show a stack trace. Don't be cute.
entries.example: Error-copy when copying to the clipboard fails.

entries.meaning: Outline only. A heading and one line under each.
entries.when: You want structure before prose.
entries.avoid: Don't draft the full piece.
entries.example: Skeleton for a practical-exam study sheet.

entries.meaning: Turn the output into bullet points.
entries.when: A list will be scanned, not read as prose.
entries.avoid: Don't use a bullet for a single sentence that should stay prose.
steps: No nested bullets unless the nesting is real.
entries.example: Bullets for how to use this book.

entries.meaning: Give the shortest useful summary.
entries.when: Someone needs the point before the detail.
entries.avoid: Don't omit the caveat that changes the action.
steps: The action, if there is one.
The caveat, if skipping it would mislead.
entries.example: Tldr what this command book is for.

entries.meaning: Turn this into a checklist. One action per line.
entries.when: A person is about to do the steps, not read about them.
entries.avoid: Don't combine two actions on one line.
steps: Order them the way the work happens.
entries.example: Checklist for shipping a small UI change.

entries.meaning: Design the screen as a product: hierarchy, one primary action, real states.
entries.when: A screen is new or feels like a wireframe.
entries.avoid: Don't add a second accent. Don't decorate.
steps: Hierarchy through size, weight, and color.
Empty, busy, and error states if those exist.
entries.example: UI for the command list on a phone.

entries.meaning: Use the existing color, type, and spacing.
entries.when: A new surface is drifting from the product.
entries.avoid: Don't invent a palette. Don't add a new font.
steps: If a value is missing, add a token. Don't sprinkle a one-off.
entries.example: Tokens only. No new colors for the agent book.

entries.meaning: Set the regions, what is primary, and what collapses on a phone.
entries.when: The desktop layout doesn't have a phone plan.
entries.avoid: Don't hide the primary action below a long rail on a phone.
steps: Say what stacks on a narrow screen.
entries.example: Layout: groups as a rail on a laptop, chips on a phone.

entries.meaning: Say what moves, how far, and how long. Honor reduced motion.
entries.when: Something animates, or you're about to add motion.
entries.avoid: Don't animate layout. Don't bounce.
steps: Opacity and transform only, unless there's a reason.
Reduced motion gets an instant or opacity-only change.
entries.example: Motion for the detail sheet.

entries.meaning: Review the work and point out what needs improvement.
entries.when: You want a critique of a screen or a flow.
entries.avoid: Don't restyle it in the critique. Name the smallest fix.
steps: The smallest fix for each real problem.
Leave taste comments out unless they block use.
entries.example: Critique the command list.

entries.meaning: Hold the name, palette, and type. Don't restyle the product in passing.
entries.when: A change is threatening to rebrand the app.
entries.avoid: Don't introduce a new logo, accent, or voice.
steps: Keep the existing name and tokens.
Match the voice of the existing copy.
entries.example: Brand stays Cuebook. This is a second book, not a new product.

entries.meaning: List every state of this screen and what the person can do in each.
entries.when: A screen has more modes than the mock shows.
entries.avoid: Don't design only the full list.
entries.example: States: all commands, one group, search, saved, empty, detail open, brief full.

entries.meaning: Specify the share card: the sentence, the picture, and the card type.
entries.when: The link will be shared and needs a card.
entries.avoid: Don't promise a picture you don't have.
entries.example: Og for Cuebook.

entries.meaning: Direct one still: subject, light, and what must stay recognizable.
entries.when: You want a single image direction, not a menu of moods.
entries.avoid: Don't add people, logos, or text you weren't given.
steps: Name the light and the lens feel.
entries.example: Still of the product on a wood table, north window, no extra props.

entries.meaning: Four distinct directions for the same subject, labeled, so one can be picked.
entries.when: You haven't chosen a direction yet.
entries.avoid: Don't produce four near-duplicates.
steps: Say how they differ in one line.
entries.example: Contact sheet for a clinic hero. Same room, four lights.

entries.meaning: Change only what is specified in the uploaded image.
entries.when: An image exists and should be edited, not restaged.
entries.avoid: Don't change identity, pose, or background unless the instruction says so.
steps: If an edit would require inventing a fact, skip it and say so.
entries.example: Edit-img: remove the outlet on the back wall. Leave the person alone.

entries.meaning: Direct one clip: start, action, end, camera. One motion.
entries.when: You want a short moving shot.
entries.avoid: Don't stack three ideas in one clip.
entries.example: Clip: the goniometer settles on the joint. One slow push-in. No text.

entries.meaning: A clean hero image with the subject as the focal point.
entries.when: You need a primary picture for a page or a card.
entries.avoid: Don't add a headline you weren't given. Don't crowd the subject.
steps: Leave clean space only if a line of type was provided.
entries.example: Hero of the instrument on a dark field. No slogan.

entries.meaning: A user-style photo or clip, as if someone is showing it to a friend.
entries.when: You want it to feel handheld, not like an ad.
entries.avoid: Don't polish it into a studio shot.
entries.example: Ugc of the product on a kitchen counter, phone photo.

entries.meaning: Use only the labels and facts provided. Leave off anything else.
entries.when: The image needs words and the words must be true.
entries.avoid: Don't invent measurements, prices, or anatomy.
steps: If a label wasn't supplied, don't add one.
entries.example: Labels: only 'Knee flexion' and '120°'. Nothing else.

entries.meaning: Treat pasted picture-book tokens as shorthand. Follow each meaning.
entries.when: You are combining visual codes from the other book.
entries.avoid: They are not secret switches. Don't obey the token if you ignore the meaning.
steps: If a code wants a fact you don't have, omit it.
entries.example: Codes: /packshot and /northlight. Subject is the bottle I uploaded.

entries.meaning: Open the URL and report the title and the main content.
entries.when: You need to know what's on a page.
entries.avoid: Don't describe the browser chrome. Don't click yet.
steps: Open the URL you were given.
entries.example: Open the docs page I pasted.

entries.meaning: Extract the fields named. Mark a field missing rather than guessing.
entries.when: The page has facts you want pulled out.
entries.avoid: Don't fill a blank with a plausible value.
entries.example: Extract name, date, and location from this page.

entries.meaning: Do these steps in order. After each one, say what you see.
entries.when: You have a known path through a site.
entries.avoid: Don't improvise if a step isn't on the page. Stop.
steps: After each step, one line on what you see.
Stop if the page disagrees with the step.
entries.example: Click-path: open the docs, then the API section, then authentication.

entries.meaning: Describe the screen that proves this step worked.
entries.when: You need evidence of a page state.
entries.avoid: Don't describe what you hoped to see. Describe what is there.
steps: Say whether it matches the expected step.
entries.example: Shot after the form submits.

entries.meaning: Fill only the fields provided. Don't submit unless told.
entries.when: A form needs specific values.
entries.avoid: Don't invent a password, a card, or an address. Don't submit on your own.
steps: Stop before submit unless the task says submit.
entries.example: Form: email is the one I gave you. Don't submit.

entries.meaning: Wait until the condition named, or say it timed out.
entries.when: The page is changing and the next step depends on it.
entries.avoid: Don't click around while you wait.
steps: If it doesn't, say it timed out and what you do see.
entries.example: Watch until the results table has more than one row.

entries.meaning: Stay in the current browser session. Don't open a second one.
entries.when: A session is already signed in or already on the right site.
entries.avoid: Don't launch a fresh profile.
steps: If you can't see it, say so. Don't start another.
entries.example: Session stays on the browser that's already open.

entries.meaning: Don't try to sign in. If a wall appears, stop and describe it.
entries.when: The page may ask for an account and you don't want one used.
entries.avoid: Don't type credentials. Don't click through a login with a guess.
steps: If the content is public, read it.
If a sign-in wall appears, stop.
entries.example: No-login. Just read the public pricing page.

entries.meaning: Teach it as a lesson: the idea, a concrete case, the usual mistake.
entries.when: You want to learn the thing, not just get an answer.
entries.avoid: Don't dump the whole chapter. Don't quiz yet unless another command says so.
entries.example: Teachme end feel versus a hard stop.

entries.meaning: Ask one question. Wait for the answer. Then mark it.
entries.when: You want to be tested, not handed the list.
entries.avoid: Don't ask the next question in the same message. Don't give the answer before the attempt.
entries.example: Quizme on goniometer alignment for knee flexion.

entries.meaning: Set the station, ask for the step, then correct the performance.
entries.when: You want a practical rep, not a lecture.
entries.avoid: Don't demonstrate the whole skill and call it a drill.
steps: Set the scene: position, landmarks, what you can see.
entries.example: Drill manual muscle test for hip abduction. I'm the student.

entries.meaning: Play the examiner. One check-off question, then grade it against the standard.
entries.when: You want the pressure of a practical, including the grading.
entries.avoid: Don't soften a wrong answer into a pass. Don't ask three questions at once.
steps: Grade it: pass, borderline, or miss, with the standard you used.
entries.example: Oral me on ankle dorsiflexion. Examiner voice.

entries.meaning: From what I show you, name the gaps. Don't pad.
entries.when: You want to know what is missing before a test.
entries.avoid: Don't reteach topics I already have cold.
steps: Say which gap to close first.
entries.example: Gaps: I can landmark the knee but I rush the end feel.

entries.meaning: One memory hook, tied to the real mechanism.
entries.when: A list won't stick and you want one hook.
entries.avoid: Don't use a cute story that isn't how the thing works.
steps: Say where the hook would mislead you if you trusted it too far.
entries.example: Mnemonic for the order of a MMT grade.

entries.meaning: Teach by asking guided questions.
entries.when: You want to arrive at the idea, not be handed it.
entries.avoid: Don't ask a question you immediately answer.
steps: Ask the question that unlocks the next step.
Use the answer to choose the next question.
entries.example: Socratic through why the axis goes over the joint.

entries.meaning: Force a sequential, ordered explanation.
entries.when: Order matters and a summary would hide it.
entries.avoid: Don't skip a step because it seems obvious.
steps: Name the check at the end of the sequence.
entries.example: Stepbystep for measuring ankle dorsiflexion.

entries.meaning: List the common misunderstandings about this topic.
entries.when: You want the traps before you practice.
entries.avoid: Don't include straw men. These should be mistakes people actually make.
steps: How you'd notice it in a practical.
entries.example: Misconceptions about end feel.

entries.meaning: Explain it as simply as possible, to test whether it is actually understood.
entries.when: You want the simple version as a test of understanding.
entries.avoid: Don't hide behind jargon. Don't lose the mechanism.
steps: The one place the plain version is incomplete.
entries.example: Feynman gait during stance.

entries.meaning: Three different alternatives. For each, the upside, the cost, and when it is the wrong pick.
entries.when: You have not chosen and want real options.
entries.avoid: Don't offer three wordings of the same option.
steps: Upside, cost, and the case where it is wrong.
Don't pick yet unless another command says to decide.
entries.example: Alt3 for saving a brief: this device, an account, or no save.

entries.meaning: Compare two or more options side by side.
entries.when: The options exist and you want them lined up.
entries.avoid: Don't add a recommendation unless asked. Comparison first.
steps: Use a table if there are more than two criteria.
Leave the call for /decide if it wasn't requested.
entries.example: Compare starring on device versus a written list.

entries.meaning: Make the call. Say why, and what would change it.
entries.when: You want a decision, not a survey.
entries.avoid: Don't hand the choice back. Don't hide the condition that would flip it.
entries.example: Decide whether the agent book should open by default.

entries.meaning: Identify the risks that can actually happen, each with a mitigation you can do now.
entries.when: You are about to commit to a plan.
entries.avoid: Don't list generic risks. Don't mitigate with 'be careful.'
steps: Risks that can happen on this task.
Drop risks you cannot act on.
entries.example: Riskmap for storing the brief in local storage.

entries.meaning: Identify the hidden assumptions in the claim or the plan.
entries.when: Something sounds decided but rests on unstated premises.
entries.avoid: Don't treat an assumption as a fact once you've named it.
steps: Say which one to check first.
entries.example: Assumptions in 'students will paste the whole book into the agent.'

entries.meaning: Name the tradeoff being ignored.
entries.when: A plan pretends you can have both.
entries.avoid: Don't resolve it unless asked. Name it.
steps: Name the two things in tension.
Say what you give up on each side.
entries.example: Tradeoff between a full list on one screen and a readable phone layout.

entries.meaning: Order the work. Say what drops if time runs out.
entries.when: There is more to do than will fit.
entries.avoid: Don't rank everything as high.
entries.example: Priority: command list, briefs, picture-book link, presets.

entries.meaning: Propose the smaller version that still ships the point.
entries.when: The full idea is too big for this pass.
entries.avoid: Don't cut the part that makes it the thing. Cut the ornaments.
steps: State what you are leaving out.
entries.example: Scope-cut the command book so it still counts as a full list.

entries.meaning: What failed, the cause, and the change in how we'll do it.
entries.when: A piece of work missed and you want the lesson.
entries.avoid: Don't write a blame story. Don't propose a process nobody will follow.
steps: The change in the next attempt.
entries.example: Postmortem on the last UI that looked fine in dev and broke when built.

entries.meaning: Choose one useful next action, and how to start it.
entries.when: You are stalled and need the next move, not a plan.
entries.avoid: Don't list five next steps.
steps: What done looks like for that step.
entries.example: Nextstep after the command list is in.

entries.meaning: Generate the strongest counterargument.
entries.when: You want the best case against the current plan.
entries.avoid: Don't argue a weak version so the plan still wins.
steps: State the plan in one line.
Give the strongest case against it.
Say whether that case changes the call.
entries.example: Counter: opening the agent book by default hides the picture codes.

entries.meaning: Critique aggressively to expose weaknesses.
entries.when: You want the plan stressed, not encouraged.
entries.avoid: Don't insult. Attack the plan.
steps: Stop before proposing a replacement unless asked.
entries.example: Redteam the idea of pasting twelve commands at once.

entries.meaning: Find the small set of actions that drive most of the result.
entries.when: The list of work is long and you want the few that matter.
entries.avoid: Don't pretend the rest is worthless. Say it is the rest.
steps: Say the result they get you.
Say what you are explicitly not doing first.
entries.example: Pareto for learning a joint exam this week.
